1. Look for the worklist table displayed in the center of the screen showing patient records and click a patient name to open the wheel interface.
2. Locate the "Document Viewer" button on the wheel interface — it appears as a paper/document icon — and click it.
3. Wait until the "Document Viewer" page is visible.
4. Take a screenshot of the main Document Viewer interface, ensuring the following elements are visible:
5. Verify that the left panel (Document Explorer) is fully expanded and visible.
6. Take a screenshot of the Document Explorer panel, ensuring the patient details at the top, study categories (Current, Prior, All), and the ability to manage reports/documents are clearly visible. This screenshot highlights the structured layout of the Document Explorer. Save it as `./img/documentexplorer.png`.
7. In the Document Explorer, ensure the top section with patient-specific details (e.g., name, ID, medical information) is visible.
8. Take a screenshot of the patient details section, ensuring identifiers, medical information, and any additional icons are clear. This screenshot provides a quick reference to patient details. Save it as `./img/patientdetails.png`.
9. Hover over the patient card in the left panel to expand the patient information section.
10. Take a screenshot of the patient chart with prominently displayed patient name, demographic details (e.g., age, gender), and the pop-out icon. This screenshot highlights the patient chart and its accessibility. Save it as `./img/popuppatientinfo.png`.
11. Locate the BMI measurement section within the patient chart.
12. Hover over the BMI indicator to display the tooltip with normal/abnormal status.
13. Take a screenshot of the BMI status section, ensuring the tooltip, indicator, and surrounding details are visible. This screenshot emphasizes the BMI measurement and its relevance. Save it as `./img/bmistatus.png`.
14. Scroll down to the patient card section in the left panel.
15. Take a screenshot of the patient card showing vital signs (height, weight, heart rate, blood pressure), ensuring icons and indicators are clear. This screenshot provides an overview of patient vitals. Save it as `./img/patientcards.png`.
16. Locate the "Filter Document" section in the patient document access interface.
17. Ensure the filter options (All, Uploaded Documents, Registration Forms) are visible.
18. Take a screenshot of the filter document interface, focusing on the filtering functionality and layout. This screenshot demonstrates document access and management. Save it as `./img/filterdocument.png`.
19. Locate the "Upload Document" icon in the patient document access interface.
20. Click the upload icon to open the file explorer.
21. Take a screenshot of the upload interface, ensuring the upload widget, rename option, and "Upload as" options are visible. This screenshot highlights the upload process. Save it as `./img/uploaddocument.png`.
22. Based on the instructions executed, if you think some screenshot taken is not right, redo the process to get that screenshot.
